chunks: And that He may admit men and women who believe into gardens with rivers running by, to live for ever there, and absolve their evil, -- This, in the sight of God, will be the great fulfilment --
ai.seo_question: What constitutes 'great success' (fawz 'azim) for believers according to Surah Al-Fath?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *Kaffarat al-Sayyi'at* (expiation of sins), where divine grace transforms minor misdeeds into merits for the faithful. The 'great success' (*Fawz 'Azim*) is interpreted not merely as entry into Paradise, but as the complete purification of the soul, reflecting the mercy of Allah that accompanies the spiritual victory of the believers.
